Pathologic changes in the macular region are extrafoveally located, linear RPE layer defects (lacquer cracks), potentially widening to round RPE layer defects (patchy atrophies), in some eyes with central BM defects; BM defects with RPE layer defects in the foveal region, accompanied by macular neovascularization or subsequent subretinal RPE cell proliferation ("macular atrophy"); myopic macular retinoschisis; and staphylomas. With longer axial length, the prevalence of non-glaucomatous optic neuropathy and glaucoma-like/glaucomatous optic neuropathy steeply increases beyond an axial length of 26.0-26.5 mm. With BM thickness being independent of axial length and in view of eye shape change from an oblate or sphere in emmetropia to a prolate rotational ellipsoid in myopia, the myopia specific morphological changes may be associated with a primary BM enlargement in the region peripheral to the optic disc.

records.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (F-DALK) with those of manual-trephination DALK (M-DALK) in treating keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Through November 2022, we comprehensively searched PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, and 4 Chinese databases. Studies that involved comparisons between F-DALK and M-DALK groups and that reported on relevant efficacy and/or safety parameters were included. Primary outcomes were uncorrected- and corrected-distance visual acuity and intraoperative complication rates. Secondary outcomes were spherical equivalent, topographic astigmatism, refractive cylinder, mean keratometry, endothelial cell density, suture removal time, and postoperative complication rates. These data were analyzed using Cochrane Review Manager software version 5.3.

Results

This meta-analysis included 9 nonrandomized controlled studies involving 1713 eyes. In eyes treated with F-DALK, corrected-distance visual acuity at 1 to 6 months (weighted mean difference = -0.07 [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.10 to -0.03]; I2 = 0%; P < .001) after surgery was better and intraoperative Descemet membrane perforation occurred less often (odds ratio = 0.53 [95% CI 0.31-0.92]; I2 = 6%; P = .02) than in eyes treated with M-DALK. No clinically significant differences in other outcomes were found among the groups.

Conclusions

Both F-DALK and M-DALK are safe and efficacious for patients with keratoconus. Compared with M-DALK, F-DALK can provide better early visual acuity and reduce the intraoperative perforation rate, and its likely improvements to long-term visual quality and endothelial cell preservation warrant further investigation. In addition, the 2 techniques seem to be comparable regarding refractive outcomes and other complications.

records.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
content.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is the most common cause of vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) with an increasing prevalence tied to the global epidemic in diabetes. Despite significant advances, the management of DME remains a dynamic field with many unresolved controversies. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) allows objective assessment, however, correlation between vision and morphological changes can be inconsistent, causing disagreements on treatment strategies. DME is a complex disease with multifactorial pathophysiological pathways, leading to heterogenous treatment responses. There is a lack of standardized definition of treatment "non-response" and protocol for switching to second-line or adjuvant treatments. New anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) drugs and multi-targeted therapies seem to demonstrate improved durability, but long-term data is not yet available. Research in artificial intelligence (AI) is developing rapidly, however, rigorous appraisal of its reliability and generalizability are necessary before its implementation. Significant vision loss from DME in pregnant women, young children and elderly patients with systemic comorbidities are challenging conundrums. An international panel of experts (IPE) comprising 36 experts from 16 countries formulated and voted on the consensus statements in 5 key areas: 1) Diagnostic controversies around classification and imaging; 2) Treatment controversies; 3) Management paradigm between protocol-based and individualized approaches; 4) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics and AI application, and 5) Special considerations for specific patient populations. There is an imminent need for mutual agreement on the best-possible approach to DME management in order to promote the optimal patient outcomes and to identify specific issues that require prioritization of resources and research.

records.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
content.abstract: Macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) is a rare neurodegenerative retinal disease defined by a unique combination of reduced macular pigment, a characteristic angiographic pattern, and a localized clinical presentation. The condition typically affects the temporal perifovea and leads to progressive visual impairment. No definitive treatment exists. Current management is limited to intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections for end-stage neovascular complications and the recently approved Encelto implant (Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc.), which delivers ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) for neuroprotection. To clarify the still enigmatic pathophysiology of MacTel, we conducted a comprehensive review of all human histopathology reports published in English through December 31, 2024. Findings were systematically evaluated with respect to tissue processing techniques, postmortem fixation times, disease stage at last recorded ophthalmologic evaluation, diagnostic certainty, inclusion of control specimens, and the anatomic origin of analyzed retinal sections. This approach aimed to identify histopathologic features most likely to represent core disease mechanisms. Each of the features identified as most likely to be pathophysiologically relevant was independently assessed for clinical and histopathologic specificity. These features were then further interpreted in the context of genetic, metabolic, and anatomic associations reported in the literature. Donor demographics, coexisting ocular conditions, and systemic comorbidities were also reviewed to support the development of an integrative hypothesis for MacTel pathogenesis. Drawing on this synthesis, we propose a histopathology-informed model of disease pathophysiology and outline a provisional timeline for the contribution of key factors to clinical expression. We also review current neuroprotective strategies and provide targeted recommendations for future therapeutic development and histopathologic research. The conceptual framework developed in this work -grounded in rigorous analysis of the most consistent and methodologically validated histopathologic findings, and interpretation of their mechanistic context- may serve as a model for deciphering rare retinal diseases and for generating focused, hypothesis-driven questions to guide future investigation.

records.title: Association Between Visual Acuity and Residual Retinal Fluid Following Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Association Between Visual Acuity and Residual Retinal Fluid Following Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

The association between residual subretinal fluid (SRF) and intraretinal fluid (IRF) and visual acuity following anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) treatment is not well understood.

Objective

To examine the association of residual retinal fluid, SRF, and IRF with visual acuity following anti-VEGF treatment in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Data sources

A systematic literature search was performed from January 2005 to August 2021 using Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library.

Study selection

Peer-reviewed articles reporting on visual acuity stratified by the presence or absence of any residual SRF, IRF, or any retinal fluid at last study observation after intravitreal bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept, or brolucizumab in patients with nAMD were included. Studies that were noncomparative, included fewer than 10 eyes, or reported on other anti-VEGF agents were excluded.

Data extraction and synthesis

Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and synthesis. The Cochrane risk of bias tool 2 and ROBINS-I were used to assess risk of bias and GRADE evaluation was conducted to assess certainty of evidence.

Main outcomes and measures

Primary outcomes were BCVA at last study observation, change in BCVA from baseline, and retinal thickness at last study observation.

Results

In this systematic review and meta-analysis, 11 studies (6 randomized clinical trials [RCTs]) comprising 3092 eyes were included in our analysis. Across all included studies, the BCVA of eyes with residual SRF was better than eyes without SRF (weighted mean difference [WMD], 3.1 letter score; 95% CI, 0.05 to 6.18; P = .05; GRADE, low certainty of evidence; 6 studies; 1931 eyes) but similar in RCTs (WMD, 2.7 letter score; 95% CI, -2.40 to 7.84; P = .30; GRADE, low certainty of evidence; 3 studies; 1406 eyes). The BCVA of eyes with residual IRF was worse than that of eyes without IRF (WMD, -8.2 letter score; 95% CI, -11.79 to -4.50; P < .001; GRADE, low; 7 studies; 2114 eyes).

Conclusions and relevance

The findings suggest that the presence of residual SRF was associated with slightly better BCVA at last study observation; however, baseline differences in BCVA existed and this conclusion was primarily driven by 1 study. The presence of residual IRF was associated with substantially worse BCVA at last study observation and less improvement of BCVA from baseline. The conclusions are limited by the inclusion of data from observational studies, heterogeneity, and a low certainty of evidence.

records.title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL HEAD-UP DISPLAY VERSUS STANDARD OPERATING MICROSCOPE FOR VITRECTOMY SURGERY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL HEAD-UP DISPLAY VERSUS STANDARD OPERATING MICROSCOPE FOR VITRECTOMY SURGERY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effects of vitrectomy with three-dimensional head-up display (3D HUD) versus standard operating microscopy (SOM) for retinal diseases.

Methods

The PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase databases were comprehensively searched to identify studies that compared 3D HUD versus SOM in vitrectomy for retinal diseases (PROSPERO protocol CRD42021265827). The primary outcomes are duration of surgical time, postoperative best-corrected visual acuity, endoillumination levels, and intraoperative complications. The secondary outcomes are reattachment rate of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, macular hole closure rate, and the like.

Results

Fifteen studies of 2,889 eyes were included. Compared with SOM, 3D HUD vitrectomy took a longer surgical time (weighted mean difference = 1.48; 95% confidence interval, 0.13-2.82), but it needed lower endoillumination levels (weighted mean difference = -16.04, 95% confidence interval, -18.33 to -13.75) than SOM. There were no significant differences in the postoperative best-corrected visual acuity, intraoperative complications, reattachment rate of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, or closure rate of macular hole.

Conclusion

Our results suggested that 3D HUD provides lower retinal illumine toxicities but with a longer surgical time. The surgical results and complications of vitrectomy were equally comparable for 3D HUD and SOM.

records.title: Elements of visuopathy of prematurity are unified by intermittent or sustained systemic inflammation.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Elements of visuopathy of prematurity are unified by intermittent or sustained systemic inflammation.
content.abstract: We hypothesize that the major pathologies associated with the visual system in preterm infants, retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), cerebral visual impairment (CVI), and neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI), are unified by a common etio-pathogenesis involving intermittent and/or sustained systemic inflammation (ISSI). We refer to the resulting adverse visual outcomes (AVO) as "visuopathy of prematurity" (VOP). We present the published evidence supporting an etio-pathogenic paradigm centered around ISSI that begins before birth (early phase 1), is exacerbated in the newborn period (intermediate phase 2), and culminates in adverse visual and neurodevelopmental outcomes (late phase 3).

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Smartphone-Based Deep Learning Exophthalmometry in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Multicenter, Multiethnic Validation Study.
records.publisher: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

content.title: Smartphone-Based Deep Learning Exophthalmometry in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Multicenter, Multiethnic Validation Study.
content.abstract:
Background

Proptosis is the principal quantitative measure of disease severity in thyroid eye disease (TED), but Hertel exophthalmometry has substantial interobserver variability and requires in-person specialist visits. Existing deep learning (DL) proptosis-from-photograph models require studio-acquired images. We aimed to validate, in a multicenter multiethnic study, a DL model fine-tuned to estimate proptosis (mm) from nonstudio facial photographs-smartphone selfies or clinician-taken photographs.

Methods

This validation study included 361 patients with confirmed or suspected TED at three institutions. Data were collected prospectively at two Korean sites-Severance Hospital (SH; 203 patients/3654 facial images; internal validation) and Seoul National University Bundang Hospital (SNUBH; 79/933; same-ethnicity external validation)-and retrospectively, from routine-care images, at one Spanish site, Virgen Macarena University Hospital (HUVM; 79/336; different-ethnicity external validation). Korean patients self-acquired selfies on six smartphone models per site using a capture-guidance application; Spanish images were clinician-acquired during routine care without such guidance. The model-a dual-stream ResNet-18 jointly processing a facial image and a per-pixel depth map (ZoeDepth)-outputs a proptosis estimate (mm) per eye from one photograph and was fine-tuned, from a previously published model trained on studio digital single-lens reflex photographs, for these nonstudio acquisitions. Hertel measurements by oculoplastic specialists served as the reference standard.

Results

On single-image analysis, the mean absolute error (MAE) versus Hertel measurement was 1.14 mm (Pearson correlation coefficient [PCC] 0.83) in SH, 1.44 mm (PCC 0.85) in SNUBH, and 1.58 mm (PCC 0.77) in HUVM, with predictions within 2 mm of Hertel in 83.6%, 71.3%, and 69.7% of images, respectively. Performance was consistent across 12 smartphone models (per-device MAE 1.11-1.54 mm). For detecting severe proptosis (Hertel ≥21 mm), the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.94 (confidence interval 0.93-0.96), 0.91 (0.89-0.92), and 0.86 (0.82-0.91) in SH, SNUBH, and HUVM, respectively. Bland-Altman analysis revealed underestimation at the upper extreme.

Conclusions

An artificial intelligence model fine-tuned for nonstudio facial photographs achieved Hertel-level agreement and reliable severity discrimination across 2 ethnicities and 12 smartphones, both for patient self-acquired smartphone selfies and for clinician-acquired routine clinic photographs, providing a scalable approach for patient-facing and clinic-based monitoring of TED severity, pending further longitudinal validation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.

content.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

To evaluate the feasibility of a quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-structured reporting pipeline that integrates quantitative MRI software with large language models (LLMs) for structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers and generating clinician-facing report conclusions.

Materials and methods

A total of 192 patients with 3D T1 and 2D or 3D FLAIR MRI images from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative database were randomly selected. A deep-learning model generated structured report findings based on nine indices related to brain atrophy, white matter hyperintensities, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) space abnormalities, and compared with neuroradiologist-generated reference reports. Four LLMs (GPT-OSS 20B, MedGemma 4B, Phi-3, and Llama 3.1 8B) generated clinician-facing conclusions from the structured findings. Generated conclusions were evaluated using a five-point Likert scale across four metrics (accuracy, relevance, clarity, and satisfaction). Output errors were assessed across four categories: language, omission, addition, and numeric errors.

Results

Structured report findings demonstrated high accuracy for CSF space analysis (77.6%-97.9%). Performance for ordinal visual scales was lower under strict matching (27.1%-57.8%) but improved with a one-grade tolerance (91.7%-97.4%). Among LLMs, GPT achieved the highest scores across most metrics (median score 5) and exhibited the lowest output error rates. Smaller models (Phi-3 and Llama 3.1 8B) showed overall lower performance, with more language, omission, and addition errors. MedGemma demonstrated intermediate performance, but the highest rate of numeric errors.

Conclusion

Our quantitative MRI-to-structured reporting pipeline, integrating quantitative MRI software with LLM-based conclusion generation, might be feasible for automated structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers.

records.title: Histopathological Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Gleason Grading: A Brief Review of Prostate Cancer.
records.publisher: Journal of clinical practice and research

content.title: Histopathological Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Gleason Grading: A Brief Review of Prostate Cancer.
content.abstract:
Objective

Prostate cancer, one of the most common cancers affecting men's health worldwide, ranks second among cancer-related deaths. Therefore, it represents a critical health issue, and early diagnosis is crucial. Several imaging and analytical methods are used to diagnose this condition.

Materials and methods

This study focuses on research conducted between 2021 and 2025 that analyzes, diagnoses, and grades prostate cancer based on histopathological images using machine learning and deep learning algorithms. In this context, the reviewed studies also include an analysis of findings related to preprocessing and feature extraction methods that may aid in prostate cancer detection, as well as the classifiers used.

Results

According to the findings of the reviewed studies, artificial intelligence-supported prostate cancer detection systems demonstrate high clinical performance and significantly improve the diagnostic accuracy of pathologists by enabling rapid diagnosis. The presented research findings indicate a need for comprehensive studies focusing on prostate cancer using histopathological images.

Conclusion

The integration of artificial intelligence is transforming prostate cancer pathology from a traditional and subjective process into a data-driven and standardized framework. This systematic analysis of histopathological images will make significant contributions to future prostate cancer research, help achieve more reliable results in clinical decision-making processes, and lay the groundwork for personalized medicine.

records.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.

content.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.
content.abstract:
Background

Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests.

Methods

A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation.

Results

For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54-0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37-0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33-0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss' κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively).

Conclusion

The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects over 366 million adults and 139 million children worldwide, yet diagnosis remains fundamentally subjective, relying on clinical interviews, behavioral observations, and rating scales that yield inconsistent results across practitioners and settings. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) offer a paradigm shift toward objective, data-driven diagnosis by detecting complex patterns across neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and digital biomarkers that elude conventional assessment. Although AI-based ADHD research has grown exponentially, no comprehensive synthesis examines the full spectrum of data modalities, validation practices, and clinical translation readiness. This gap limits our understanding of which approaches are most promising for real-world implementation.

Objective

This scoping review will visually map the current evidence on AI-based ADHD classification with respect to predictive accuracy, data forms, data features, generalizability, and interpretability of models.

Methods

This scoping review will use the Joanna Briggs Institute approach to scoping reviews and follow the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Five electronic databases (IEEE Xplore, Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library) will be systematically searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Empirical studies in English involving the use of AI, ML, DL, or explainable AI to diagnose ADHD with a total sample size greater than 100 participants (ADHD and control groups combined) and a non-ADHD control group (individuals with typical development or healthy individuals) will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen the titles, abstracts, and full texts, and any conflicts will be resolved through either discussion or arbitration. A standardized Microsoft Excel template will be used to extract data that will include the following: bibliographic data, data modalities, data models, data validation approaches, performance metrics, and explainability approaches. Thematic and narrative analysis will be used to synthesize findings on 4 research questions that will address model performance, data modality contributions, data characteristics, and interpretability methods.

Results

The scoping review began in December 2025. Analysis and screening are in progress, with the scoping review expected to be completed and submitted for publication in June 2026.

Conclusions

This scoping review will provide the first comprehensive synthesis of AI-, ML-, and DL-based ADHD diagnostic classification studies, mapping the evidence across data modalities, validation practices, interpretability methods, and clinical translation readiness. Findings will inform future methodological standards and support the translation of AI-based diagnostic tools into clinical practice.

records.title: The Influence of Large Language Model-Generated Artificial Intelligence Risk Estimates on Clinical Decision-Making in Breast Imaging: A Simulation-Based Study.

content.title: The Influence of Large Language Model-Generated Artificial Intelligence Risk Estimates on Clinical Decision-Making in Breast Imaging: A Simulation-Based Study.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision-support tools in radiology, yet their influence on clinical decision-making remains a significant concern. This study evaluates how artificial intelligence (AI)-generated malignancy risk estimates influence clinical decisions in breast imaging and assesses automation bias (AB) among radiology residents at different training levels. Methods: In this simulation-based study, 20 residents reviewed radiology reports for 15 synthetic breast imaging cases generated by ChatGPT-4 Turbo, each presented in either a concordant or discordant format. Participants were stratified into two groups based on their completion of a breast imaging rotation and evaluated each case by assigning a BI-RADS score, recommending management, and rating their confidence in the AI risk estimate. Diagnostic accuracy and independent predictors of AB were analyzed using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) to account for reader-level clustering. Results: Overall management accuracy was significantly lower in cases with discordant AI outputs (p = 0.008). A similar, albeit non-significant, decreasing trend was observed for BI-RADS accuracy. While advanced residents maintained high management accuracy regardless of AI concordance, early-stage residents showed a sharp decline in discordant cases (77.3% vs. 45.3%; p = 0.006). This decline was most critical in malignant cases for early-stage residents, where accuracy dropped from 92.0% to 48.0% (p < 0.001). In the multivariable GEE logistic regression model, training level was the only independent predictor of AB (OR: 0.09, 95% CI: 0.03-0.28, p < 0.001). Conclusions: In this simulation study, advanced clinical training was associated with lower susceptibility to AB in breast imaging, although training level alone is unlikely to be a sufficient safeguard. Safe integration of AI tools will require caution among junior trainees alongside system-level measures such as model transparency and institutional oversight.

records.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

records.title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections.
records.publisher: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

content.title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections.
content.abstract:
Background

Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection.

Methods

We systematically compared six deep learning models, including the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) series and the Detection Transformer (DETR). Three evaluation datasets were constructed. Datasets 1 and 2 (derived from 4000 hyphae and 4500 spore images) were used to assess image-level detection using sensitivity, precision and F1 score. Dataset 1 was manually annotated for the YOLO series and DETR; Dataset 2 (unannotated) served as the CNN series' benchmark. Dataset 3 (1, 870 specimens from 1, 730 patients) was used to evaluate sample-level performance via confusion matrix analysis for the YOLO series and DETR models, employing medical records as the reference standard. The best-performing model was optimized and deployed into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform for real-time clinical decision support.

Results

YOLOv11 outperformed all other evaluated architectures. Detection was generally better at 400× than at 200× magnification. Notably, the F1 score for hyphae detection by YOLOv11 increased from 90.42% (200×) to 92.06% (400×). All models achieved higher accuracy for spores than hyphae. Patient-level confusion-matrix analysis confirmed YOLOv11 superiority. After optimizing an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.25 and the maximum confidence (Cmax) strategy, 200× hyphae F1 rose to 97.84% and the positive predictive value (PPV) to 98.27%. Subgroup analysis showed robust performance across different diseases, with tinea capitis reaching the highest F1 score (98.53%).

Conclusion

The optimized YOLOv11 model demonstrates potential as a rapid and standardized supportive tool for the microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections. Integration into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform demonstrates the feasibility of real-time AI-assisted fungal detection, offering a standardized tool to support clinical decision-making. This work supports AI as a potential complement to clinical and laboratory expertise, pending further validation in prospective and multi-center settings, and highlights its potential to streamline fungal infection diagnostic workflows.

records.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.

content.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep learning models or raw waveform ECGs produced similar findings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review Informed by a Systematic Search.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review Informed by a Systematic Search.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of mortality, and early identification of phenotypes, exacerbation risk, and treatment response remains challenging. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for improving prediction, classification, and monitoring in COPD. This narrative review, informed by a systematic search, evaluated current AI applications in COPD management.

Methods

The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024502765) and reported with reference to PRISMA 2020 principles. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to May 2025. Eligible studies applied Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Deep Learning approaches to adult COPD populations for diagnostic, prognostic, monitoring, phenotyping, or disease management purposes. Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers, and methodological quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools.

Results

Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. AI demonstrated high discriminative accuracy for COPD diagnosis, exacerbation prediction, and mortality risk (mean Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve [AUROC] = 0.83), although methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation were common. Models integrating multimodal data generally outperformed single-domain approaches. Risk-of-bias assessment identified concerns related to small sample sizes, limited external validation, and incomplete reporting of model development and validation procedures.

Conclusion

Current evidence suggests that AI may support COPD diagnosis, prognostic prediction, and telemonitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, and inconsistent reporting standards continue to limit clinical translation. Further high-quality, externally validated studies are needed to support implementation in respiratory care.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Ischemic Stroke Detection in Non-contrast CT: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Ischemic Stroke Detection in Non-contrast CT: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objective

We aim to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to objectively assess the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) models for detecting ischemic stroke (IS) in non-contrast CT (NCCT), and to compare the diagnostic performance between AI and clinicians.

Materials and methods

Until February 2025, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, IEEE Xplore, and Embase for studies using AI based on NCCT images from human subjects for IS detection or classification. The risk of bias was evaluated using the prediction model study risk of bias assessment tool (PROBAST). For meta-analysis, the pooled sensitivities, specificities, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves were used.

Results

A total of 38 studies, with 74 trials extracted from 32 studies were included. For AI performance, the pooled sensitivity and specificity were 91.2% (95%CI: 87.6%-93.8%) and 96.0% (95%CI: 93.6%-97.6%) for internal validation and 59.8% (95%CI:39.9%-76.9%) and 97.3% (95%CI: 93.2%-98.9%) for external validation. For clinicians' performance, the pooled sensitivity and specificity were 44.1% (95%CI: 33.8%-55.0%) and 85.5% (95%CI: 68.4%-94.1%) for internal validation and 46.1% (95%CI: 31.5%-61.3%) and 83.6% (95%CI: 62.8%-93.9%) for external validation. The pooled sensitivity and specificity increased to 83.7% (95%CI: 53.0%-95.9%) and 86.7% (95%CI: 77.1%-92.6%) for clinicians with AI assistance. The subgroup analysis results indicated that higher model sensitivity was associated with the data augmentation (93.9%, 95%CI: 90.2%-96.2%) and transfer learning (94.7%, 95%CI: 92.0%-96.6%). There were 22 of 38 (58%) studies that were judged to have high risk of bias. Sensitive analysis and subgroup analysis identified multiple sources of heterogeneity in the data, including risk of bias and AI model types.

Conclusion

Our study reveals that AI has an acceptable performance in detecting IS in NCCT in internal validation, although significant heterogeneity was observed in the meta-analysis. However, the generalizability and practical applicability of AI in real-world clinical settings remain limited due to insufficient external validation.

records.title: Effectiveness of Platelet-Rich Plasma in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness of Platelet-Rich Plasma in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Knee osteoarthritis (OA) causes chronic pain and disability, with limited benefit from conventional treatments. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed as a biologic therapy with potential tissue-repair properties; however, its clinical efficacy remains uncertain.

Objective

To assess the effectiveness of intra-articular PRP injections in reducing pain and improving function in patients with knee OA.

Methodology

This systematic review and meta-analysis included randomized controlled trials comparing intra-articular PRP with placebo or no treatment. Pain outcomes were measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), while functional outcomes were assessed using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) or Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS).

Results

PRP significantly reduced pain and improved function compared with placebo across short-, mid-, and long-term follow-up. The magnitude of benefit varied but remained clinically relevant.

Conclusion

PRP provides significant improvements in pain relief and functional outcomes compared with placebo or no treatment in patients with knee OA, supporting its potential as a therapeutic option. Standardized protocols and larger RCTs are warranted to further confirm its clinical effectiveness.

records.title: Effect of different acupuncture modalities on sex hormone levels in perimenopausal women: a network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effect of different acupuncture modalities on sex hormone levels in perimenopausal women: a network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Acupuncture, a common intervention in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), has been widely applied for regulating hormonal fluctuations in perimenopausal women. However, the efficacy of various acupuncture modalities is not comprehensively compared. This network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluated the effects of different acupuncture approaches on sex hormone levels, specifically estradiol (E2), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and luteinizing hormone (LH), in perimenopausal women.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and the VIP Database were searched until March 17, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on acupuncture interventions for perimenopausal women were included. The risk of bias was assessed for included studies, and data were synthesized based on a Bayesian NMA framework.

Results

36 studies on 1, 480 participants were included. Compared with control interventions, acupoint application (AA) and acupuncture therapy (AT) significantly reduced Kupperman scores. In terms of FSH reduction, AA, abdominal moxibustion (AM), and AT were superior to control. For LH, AA, AT, and AM demonstrated notable reductions compared with control. As for E2 elevation, AA, AT, and compression acupuncture (PN) achieved statistically significant improvements.

Conclusions

AM, AT, and AA significantly improved Kupperman scores, with AM being the most effective. Catgut implantation acupoint (CA) and PN showed significant effects in reducing FSH levels, followed by AT and AM, whereas plum blossom needling exhibited the greatest efficacy in increasing E2 levels. Overall, acupuncture presents a promising non-pharmacological strategy for modulating hormonal balance and alleviating menopausal symptoms in perimenopausal women.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251066613.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in varicose veins: Comparative insights from other vascular diseases, evidence gaps, and future prospects.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in varicose veins: Comparative insights from other vascular diseases, evidence gaps, and future prospects.
content.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in varicose veins (VV), covering applications in image recognition, postoperative management, risk factor and biomarker analysis, and the use of large language models (LLMs) to aid clinical decision-making. While significant advancements have been made, valuable lessons can be drawn from AI applications in other vascular diseases. Key considerations for advancing AI in VV include ensuring methodological rigor, high quality data, external validation, strict attention to data security and legal standards, and linking AI tools to clinically important outcomes. It is recommended that machine learning models be developed and validated within standardized frameworks that future VV research can adopt. Accordingly, the development of clear guidelines and benchmarks is imperative. LLMs hold promise in relieving clinicians of repetitive routine tasks, thereby enhancing diagnostic accuracy and assisting in treatment planning. Additionally, LLM-based tools could support the curation of medical content on short video platforms and assist clinicians in creating educational materials, ultimately improving patient engagement and understanding.

records.title: Predictive factors of permanent hypothyroidism after subacute thyroiditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Predictive factors of permanent hypothyroidism after subacute thyroiditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Subacute thyroiditis (SAT) is a self-limiting thyroid inflammatory disorder, but some patients develop permanent hypothyroidism, impacting long-term health. We aimed to systematically synthesize evidence on factors associated with permanent hypothyroidism after SAT.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science was conducted up to August 2025. Randomized trials, cohort, and case-control studies evaluating predictors of permanent hypothyroidism after SAT were included. Data were extracted following PRISMA guidelines, and study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Random-effects models were preferentially applied given expected clinical heterogeneity, with heterogeneity quantified using I2 and τ2.

Results

Ten studies involving 1294 patients were included. Higher free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels (mean difference = 1.85, 95% CI: 0.60-3.09; Z = 2.91, P = 0.004; I² = 0%) and positive thyroglobulin antibodies (TgAb) (OR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.35-4.88, P = 0.004; I² = 57%, τ² = 0.13) were significantly associated with an increased risk of permanent hypothyroidism after SAT. Corticosteroid therapy was associated with a lower odds of permanent hypothyroidism compared with NSAID-based management (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.23-0.70, P = 0.001; I² = 36%).

Conclusions

FT3, TgAb positivity and treatment modality are associated with the risk of permanent hypothyroidism following SAT. Compared with NSAID-based management, corticosteroid therapy is associated with lower odds of developing permanent hypothyroidism. These findings support early identification of high-risk patients and personalized follow-up strategies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420251064643.

records.title: Combined noninvasive brain stimulation and acupuncture for post-stroke motor recovery: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Combined noninvasive brain stimulation and acupuncture for post-stroke motor recovery: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Stroke is highly prevalent among older adults, and age-related reductions in neuroplastic reserve may limit motor recovery. This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to compare and rank the effects of noninvasive brain stimulation combined with acupuncture on post-stroke motor recovery, spasticity, balance, and activities of daily living (ADL).

Methods

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang, and CQVIP were searched from inception to July 1, 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating noninvasive brain stimulation, including TMS-based NIBS or transcranial direct current stimulation, combined with acupuncture or electroacupuncture were included. Pairwise and frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and confidence in network estimates was evaluated using CINeMA.

Results

Forty-six randomized controlled trials involving 4,080 participants were included. Combined interventions generally showed greater effects than single-modality therapies or conventional rehabilitation, although heterogeneity was substantial. In the network meta-analysis, both TMS-based NIBS plus acupuncture and tDCS plus acupuncture showed favorable ranking probabilities across several outcomes. tDCS plus acupuncture ranked highly for FMA total, FMA-UE, and ADL, whereas TMS-based NIBS plus acupuncture ranked favorably for FMA-LE, spasticity, and balance. Differences between the two combined regimens were generally not statistically significant. CINeMA indicated moderate, low, or very low confidence across network estimates, with no high-confidence evidence.

Conclusion

Combined noninvasive brain stimulation and acupuncture may provide additional benefits for post-stroke motor and functional recovery. However, current findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity, sparse evidence for some intervention nodes, risk-of-bias concerns, and limited confidence in several network estimates.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251051398, Identifier: CRD420251051398.

records.title: Microalbuminuria in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: The Indian journal of medical research

content.title: Microalbuminuria in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Background and objectives We conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the prevalence of microalbuminuria in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and its association with COPD severity. Methods We conducted a literature search in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and the Virtual Health Library from inception to December 31th, 2024. The search strategy was: ('chronic obstructive pulmonary disease' OR COPD OR 'chronic airflow obstruction' OR emphysema OR 'chronic bronchitis') AND (microalbuminuria OR albuminuria OR proteinuria OR 'urinary albumin creatinine ratio' OR 'urinary albumin excretion'). We included studies recruiting patients diagnosed by spirometry and providing data of microalbuminuria prevalence. We excluded studies in patients with other respiratory diseases associated with COPD, and studies published in predatory journals. The pooled prevalence of microalbuminuria was calculated using the DerSimonian-Laird binary random effects method, and the association of microalbuminuria with COPD and its severity was assessed using the Mantel-Haenszel random effects method. Results Twenty-five articles were included. The prevalence of microalbuminuria in patients with COPD was 49.3% [95% confidence interval (CI) 34.3-64.4%], which was higher than in the control population, with an estimated odds ratio of 3.94 (95% CI 2.25-6.60). In patients with severe to very severe COPD, it was higher than in those with mild to moderate COPD, with an estimated odds ratio of 4.55 (95%IC 2.85-7.28). Patients with COPD and microalbuminuria had an estimated decrease in PaO2 of 9.98 mmHg (95% CI 13.94-6.02) and an increase in PaCO2 of 8.08 mmHg (95% CI: 4.87-11.29). Interpretations and conclusions Microalbuminuria is highly prevalent in patients with COPD, with a much higher frequency than in the general population. It is more common in patients with more severe airflow obstruction and is associated with hypoxia and hypercapnia.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Graph Methods for Microbiome Research: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Graph Methods for Microbiome Research: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: The complexity of high-throughput sequencing data in microbiome research necessitates advanced analytical methods to decipher microbial community structures and interactions. Graph-based methods, which model taxa as nodes and their relationships as edges, have emerged as a powerful framework for this purpose. However, the rapid evolution of these techniques, from classical network analysis to modern graph representation learning, has created a fragmented and complex methodological landscape. This systematic review provides a comprehensive synthesis and structured overview of the field. We systematically review the literature and propose a three-part classification to categorize the primary contribution of each study: (1) novel methods for microbial network representation, (2) applications of classical graph analysis, and (3) the emerging use of graph representation learning for predictive modeling. We summarize the most frequent applications within each class, including keystone species identification, community clustering, and graph-based disease classification. Furthermore, we identify critical cross-cutting challenges, such as the lack of standardized tools and the need for improved model interpretability. By structuring the current landscape of graph-based methods, this review serves as a crucial guide for researchers to select appropriate models and highlights key gaps to direct future research.

records.title: [Artificial intelligence as decision support tool in urological oncology: current evidence and challenges].

content.title: [Artificial intelligence as decision support tool in urological oncology: current evidence and challenges].
content.abstract:
Background

The rising incidence of cancer, increasing life expectancy and complex personalized treatment concepts pose considerable challenges for the healthcare system. Artificial intelligence (AI)-in particular machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs)-offers promising potential for supporting therapeutic decisions in urological oncology.

Objective

The aim of this review is to present the current state of research on the application of AI in treatment decisions in urological oncology. For this purpose, a systematic review of publications in the PubMed database was carried out. Methodological approaches, performance indicators and challenges with regard to clinical implementation were analysed comparatively.

Results

Depending on the entity and treatment category, ML models achieve F1-scores between 0.75 and 0.99. Large language models that access external knowledge sources using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) demonstrate a high degree of guideline compliance, as evidence-based knowledge is specifically integrated into the treatment recommendations. The explainability of the models is mainly ensured by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analyses or transparent guideline referencing.

Conclusion

To date, the available evidence predominantly consists of proof-of-concept studies, with a particular emphasis on prostate, urothelial, and renal cell carcinoma. Clinical implementation remains limited, in particular due to a lack of prospective validation studies, unresolved data protection and technical challenges, and limited model transparency and explainability.

records.title: Hypotension Prediction Index-Guided Hemodynamic Management on Postoperative Organ Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.

content.title: Hypotension Prediction Index-Guided Hemodynamic Management on Postoperative Organ Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
content.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is a frequent occurrence during noncardiac surgery. Hypotensive episodes can compromise tissue perfusion, and cumulative exposure has been associated with adverse outcomes such as acute kidney injury (AKI), myocardial injury, and increased mortality. The Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI) is an artificial intelligence tool designed to predict hypotensive events before they occur, allowing clinicians to intervene proactively to prevent or mitigate hypotension. Although randomized trials and pooled analyses have shown its effectiveness in reducing both the incidence and duration of IOH, its impact on patient-centered outcomes remains unclear. From 1946 to August 8, 2025, we prospectively queried MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. We included randomized controlled trials in adult surgical patients with invasive arterial monitoring, comparing HPI-guided perioperative hemodynamic management to standard care. Primary outcome was postoperative AKI, and secondary outcomes were postoperative myocardial injury, pneumonia, arrhythmia, stroke, postoperative cognitive dysfunction, including delirium, surgical site infection, length of hospital stay, and mortality. Two authors independently evaluated the risk of bias according to the methods described in the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. A meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.1 software. Dichotomous data were presented as risk ratio, 95% confidence interval [CI]; continuous data were presented as mean difference, 95% CI. All results were pooled using random-effects models. Of 883 imported references, 14 studies (N = 2030) were included for final analysis. No significant difference in incidence of postoperative AKI was observed between HPI-guided management and standard care, RR = 0.87, 95% CI (0.71-1.07). Postoperative myocardial injury was significantly reduced in HPI-guided management group, RR = 0.61, 95% CI (0.39-0.96), although exclusion-based sensitivity analysis suggests that this finding may not be robust. No other significant differences were observed for hospital length of stay, arrhythmia, stroke, cognitive dysfunction (including delirium), surgical site infection, pneumonia, or mortality. Although HPI-guided management is associated with a reduction in postoperative myocardial injury, its significance does not withstand sensitivity analysis. All other postoperative complications, including AKI incidence, are not reduced in the intervention groups. This study has limitations inherent to the heterogeneity of included patient populations, surgical interventions performed, standard of care practices, and reporting of postoperative outcomes.

records.title: Rapid review on GenAI in nursing education.

content.title: Rapid review on GenAI in nursing education.
content.abstract:
Backround

The use of generative AI, as represented by ChatGPT, holds promising potential for nursing education. This manifests itself in various areas, including personalized learning, simulation training and teaching process support. However, its integration requires careful consideration of ethical implications, adaptation of curricula and a high level of digital competence on the part of teachers. Only in this way can potential risks, such as the distortion of knowledge, bias and educational inequalities, be avoided.

Methodes

Relevant publications were identified between 2019 and 2025 as part of a comprehensive literature search in the specialist databases PubMed, Embase, CINAHL and Scopus. The search was conducted using combined search terms that included the terms "generative AI", "ChatGPT" and "nursing". After removing duplicates and screening (PRISMA-guided), 140 full texts were analysed and divided into two publications. This rapid overview focuses on the topic of generative AI in nursing education.

Results

As part of the analysis of the included studies, five thematic areas were identified, which were divided into the categories of nursing education, competence development and nursing skills, implementation possibilities, examination quality and ethical considerations, and evaluated.
